pubpeer_signal_analysis.detail: The PubPeer discussion centers on concerns about the data integrity and statistical reporting in the referenced clinical trial and related studies from the same research group. Issues raised include identical standard error (SE) values across different groups and studies, which may suggest problematic statistical methods or reporting practices. One comment explains that the observed identical SEs are due to the use of ANCOVA with pooled error variance, but warns this approach can mislead readers and obscure true variability. Commenters encourage transparency through sharing of raw and group-specific data. No official authors' responses or publication status notices (such as retraction or correction) are present.

scraped_comments.summary: The PubPeer discussion centers on concerns about the data integrity and statistical reporting in the referenced clinical trial and related studies from the same research group. Issues raised include identical standard error (SE) values across different groups and studies, which may suggest problematic statistical methods or reporting practices. One comment explains that the observed identical SEs are due to the use of ANCOVA with pooled error variance, but warns this approach can mislead readers and obscure true variability. Commenters encourage transparency through sharing of raw and group-specific data. No official authors' responses or publication status notices (such as retraction or correction) are present.

comments.author: Andrew Grey
comments.comment: There are many concerns about the integrity of 172 publications by this research group, including this one. Some of the concerns are published 1. Anaesthesia 2020;75:1683–92, see Supplementary data. This paper is A77 2. Account Res 2020;28:149-61. 3. J Clin Epidemiol 2021;131:22-29. Journals and publishers were notified of these concerns in July 2019. 23 publications have an expression of concern. To our knowledge there has been no public response about any of the concerns. We think these publications are unreliable

comments.author: Dysdera arabisenen
comments.comment: [Image: table or graph with SE values for two groups] The two groups have identical SE values across all parameters. I understand that the means reflect the difference between data taken before and after the intervention period.

comments.author: Dysdera arabisenen
comments.comment: [Image: table or graph comparing SE values for FPG and HDL across groups and studies] In all 3 studies, the SE values for “adjusted change” of FPG (mg/dL) are 1.7 for both control and treated groups. Similarly, the SE values for HDL adjusted change are 1.3 in all 6 groups (across 3 studies). In each of the 3 studies, control and treated groups have different means, but identical SE values across all measures. (expression of concern)

comments.author: Dysdera arabisenen
comments.comment: Update of #2: The reason the control and treated groups have identical SE values is that ANCOVA generates a single pooled error variance. While not statistically “wrong,” this mode of presentation can be misleading — it prevents readers from assessing the actual within-group and between-group variabilities in the dataset. The authors are encouraged to share raw data, and group-specific SE data.

data.label: Does the study have an associated retraction?
data.comment: Confirmed that there was no retraction on journal page

data.label: Does the study have an associated expression of concern or other relevant post publication notice?
data.comment: While this paper has not been retracted the authors have published dubious publications, and the methods they adopted here can be misleading. As data were not shared it is not possible to rerun the analyses using different approaches. If I was working on a review, I would still include the paper if it met all inclusion criteria, but this information here would influence my critical appraisal, and I would need to acknowledge data limitations.

data.label: Is there evidence of concerning patterns in the publication history of authors?
data.comment: The first, second and last authors have quite a few retracted publications and many expressions of concern. Initially I had said I would include this paper if I was doing a review on the topic and it met inclusion criteria, but now I am not so sure. The challenge is: where do we draw the line? I suppose passing the "AI-Inspect test may in the future be used as part of the inclusion criteria - academic judgement will have to prevail nonetheless.

data.label: Are there concerns relating to the timing or absence of study registration?
data.comment: Full protocol was not available on the link provided. One month delay in registration is concerning but perhaps this was due to delays from the website? In theory I would only be slightly concerned, but when you see that the study finished in July it becomes a bigger issue. It is also concerning that the trial page was refreshed in 2019 and no additional data /progress was reported (even though the paper was published in 2016. Protocol stated that the first enrolment was on the 31st May 2015. Paper reports that 60 patients were recruited and intervention took 6 weeks, and the trial was conducted from May to July 2015 (note the start on the 31st May). Therefore, in about 8-9 weeks they recruited all patients and did the 6-week follow up, did all the analysis and wrote the whole paper in two months (the paper was submitted for publication on the 13th October). These are very tight timelines.
After checking all tabs, I have changed my mind and would rate this as serious concerns instead of some concerns.

comments.author: Andrew Grey
comments.comment:
There are many concerns about the integrity of 172 publications by this research group, including this one. Some of the concerns are published
1. Anaesthesia 2020;75:1683–92, see Supplementary data. This paper is A166
2. Account Res 2020;28:149-61.
3. J Clin Epidemiol 2021;131:22-29.
Journals and publishers were notified of these concerns in July 2019. 18 publications have an expression of concern, and 6 have been retracted. To our knowledge there has been no public response about any of the concerns. We think these publications are unreliable

data.label: Does the study have an associated retraction?
data.comment: One retracted paper from their reference list - this would not concern me much. However, there is a note of concern on the journal website as well. "Since publication of this article, serious concerns have been raised about the integrity of the reported methods, results and analysis. Responses by the leading author and ethics committees have been unsatisfactory and inconclusive; we advise readers to interpret the information presented in the article with due caution.". So the paper is not retracted, but these are serious limitations.

data.label: Does the study have an associated expression of concern or other relevant post publication notice?
data.comment: As before, journal page also has an expression of concern.

data.label: Is there evidence of concerning patterns in the publication history of authors?
data.comment: Most authors have had numerous expressions of concern.

data.label: Are there concerns relating to the timing or absence of study registration?
data.comment: Registration ok, but update in 2019 did not add any information even though paper was published in 2017. Recruitment started on the 21st December 2016, finished in February 2017. 12-week follow up, paper submitted in July 2017. Very short timescales.

I would have serious concerns about the paper even if it has not been retracted - I think this shows one of the benefits at the tool clearly. I would not trust including information from the paper in a review.

pubpeer_signal_analysis.detail: Two comments were posted regarding concerns and actions taken about the integrity of the referenced article. The first comment, by Andrew Grey, highlights broad concerns about the integrity of 172 publications by the same research group, mentioning previously published investigations, and concludes that the group's publications are considered unreliable by the commenter. A status notice of 'Expression of concern' was issued. The second comment, by Gerris caucasicus, reports the formal retraction of the article by the journal's editorial team, following an external statistical review that could not confirm the integrity of the trial design or reliability of conclusions. The retraction notice describes the process, asserts that the authors did not agree with the retraction, and cites related references. Both an 'Expression of concern' and a 'Retraction Notice' were observed for this article. No author responses were posted. No parsing errors occurred.

comments.author: Andrew Grey
comments.comment:
There are many concerns about the integrity of 172 publications by this research group, including this one. Some of the concerns are published
1. Anaesthesia 2020;75:1683–92, see Supplementary data. This paper is A22
2. Account Res 2020;28:149-61.
3. J Clin Epidemiol 2021;131:22-29.
Journals and publishers were notified of these concerns in July 2019. 23 publications have an expression of concern. To our knowledge there has been no public response about any of the concerns. We think these publications are unreliable

comments.author: Gerris caucasicus
comments.comment: **Retracted**, June 18, 2024: _We, the Editor and Publisher of The Journal of Maternal-Fetal & Neonatal Medicine, have retracted the following article:_ _Mohsen Taghizadeh, Mansooreh Samimi, Fariba Kolahdooz, Zohreh Tabassi, Mehri Jamilian & Zatollah Asemi (2015), Effect of multivitamin versus multivitamin-mineral supplementation on metabolic profiles and biomarkers of oxidative stress in pregnant women: a double-blind randomized clinical trial. The Journal of Maternal-Fetal & Neonatal Medicine, 28:11, 1336–1342, DOI: 10.3109/14767058.2014.954241_ _Following publication, significant concerns were raised by a third party [1] about the integrity of the data and the reported findings in the article._ _When approached for an explanation, the authors and their institution have been cooperative in providing some original data and documents. In order to verify the reported findings, the article and the original data provided by the authors were sent for review by an external statistical reviewer._ _Both the journal editorial team and the external statistical reviewer were unable to confirm the integrity of the trial design and the main outcome of the external review was that the article’s conclusions are unreliable. Therefore, as the editorial team no longer has confidence in the reported conclusions the decision has been made to retract the article._ _The authors listed in the publication have been informed. The authors do not agree with the retraction._ _We have been informed in our decision-making by our editorial policies and the COPE guidelines._ _The retracted article will remain online to maintain the scholarly record, but it will be digitally watermarked on each page as ‘Retracted’._ **Reference** 1. Bolland MJ, Gamble GD, Grey A, et al. Empirically generated reference proportions for baseline p values from rounded summary statistics. Anaesthesia. 2020;75(12):1685–1687. doi: 10.1111/anae.15165.

comments.author: Andrew Grey
comments.comment:
There are many concerns about the integrity of 172 publications by this research group, including this one. Some of the concerns are published
1. Anaesthesia 2020;75:1683–92, see Supplementary data. This paper is A34
2. Account Res 2020;28:149-61.
3. J Clin Epidemiol 2021;131:22-29.
Journals and publishers were notified of these concerns in July 2019. 23 publications have an expression of concern. To our knowledge there has been no public response about any of the concerns. We think these publications are unreliable

comments.author: Andrew Grey
comments.comment:
There are many concerns about the integrity of 172 publications by this research group, including this one. Some of the concerns are published
1. Anaesthesia 2020;75:1683–92, see Supplementary data. This paper is A72
2. Account Res 2020;28:149-61.
3. J Clin Epidemiol 2021;131:22-29.
Journals and publishers were notified of these concerns in July 2019. 23 publications have an expression of concern. To our knowledge there has been no public response about any of the concerns. We think these publications are unreliable

comments.author: Andrew Grey
comments.comment:
There are many concerns about the integrity of 172 publications by this research group, including this one. Some of the concerns are published
1. Anaesthesia 2020;75:1683–92, see Supplementary data. This paper is A140
2. Account Res 2020;28:149-61.
3. J Clin Epidemiol 2021;131:22-29.
Journals and publishers were notified of these concerns in July 2019. 18 publications have an expression of concern, and 6 have been retracted. To our knowledge there has been no public response about any of the concerns. We think these publications are unreliable

comments.author: Andrew Grey
comments.comment:
There are many concerns about the integrity of 172 publications by this research group, including this one. Some of the concerns are published
1. Anaesthesia 2020;75:1683–92, see Supplementary data. This paper is A164
2. Account Res 2020;28:149-61.
3. J Clin Epidemiol 2021;131:22-29.
Journals and publishers were notified of these concerns in July 2019. 18 publications have an expression of concern, and 6 have been retracted. To our knowledge there has been no public response about any of the concerns. We think these publications are unreliable

comments.comment:
There are many concerns about the integrity of 172 publications by this research group, including this one. Some of the concerns are published

2. Account Res 2020;28:149-61.

pubpeer_signal_analysis.detail: The single comment on this PubPeer page raises concerns regarding the integrity of 172 publications by the research group responsible for the paper under discussion, including the present study. The commenter lists references to previously published concerns and notes that journals and publishers were notified in July 2019, with 23 publications subsequently receiving expressions of concern. As of the time of commenting, there had been no public response to these issues, leading the commenter to question the reliability of these publications. There are no author responses or official publication status notices present on the page.

comments.author: Andrew Grey
comments.comment:
There are many concerns about the integrity of 172 publications by this research group, including this one. Some of the concerns are published
1. Anaesthesia 2020;75:1683–92, see Supplementary data. This paper is A27
2. Account Res 2020;28:149-61.
3. J Clin Epidemiol 2021;131:22-29.
Journals and publishers were notified of these concerns in July 2019. 23 publications have an expression of concern. To our knowledge there has been no public response about any of the concerns. We think these publications are unreliable

pubpeer_signal_analysis.detail: A single comment raises serious concerns about the integrity of 172 publications from the authors' research group, including the discussed article. The commenter cites references to other papers discussing these concerns and notes that several journals and publishers were notified in July 2019. Of the questioned works, 18 have received expressions of concern and 6 have been retracted. The commenter further highlights the lack of any public response from the authors regarding the issues raised, concluding with a statement that the publications in question are considered unreliable. No author responses or official publication status notices are present on the page.

comments.author: Andrew Grey
comments.comment:
There are many concerns about the integrity of 172 publications by this research group, including this one. Some of the concerns are published 1. Anaesthesia 2020;75:1683–92, see Supplementary data. This paper is A166
2. Account Res 2020;28:149-61.
3. J Clin Epidemiol 2021;131:22-29. Journals and publishers were notified of these concerns in July 2019. 18 publications have an expression of concern, and 6 have been retracted. To our knowledge there has been no public response about any of the concerns. We think these publications are unreliable

comments.author: Andrew Grey
comments.comment:
There are many concerns about the integrity of 172 publications by this research group, including this one. Some of the concerns are published
1. Anaesthesia 2020;75:1683–92, see Supplementary data. This paper is A140
2. Account Res 2020;28:149-61.
3. J Clin Epidemiol 2021;131:22-29.
Journals and publishers were notified of these concerns in July 2019. 18 publications have an expression of concern, and 6 have been retracted. To our knowledge there has been no public response about any of the concerns. We think these publications are unreliable

pubpeer_signal_analysis.detail: The PubPeer discussion focuses on significant concerns regarding the integrity of this article and others from the same research group. Key points raised relate to data discrepancies, overlapping publications without cross-reference, methodological inconsistencies (such as unmentioned metformin treatment and stratification), and potential issues regarding withheld beneficial treatments in the study's placebo group. An ethics committee investigation found insufficient evidence of data fabrication, but the article was ultimately retracted due to unreliable conclusions stemming from reporting omissions and overlapping data usage. There has been no author response on PubPeer, but disagreement with the retraction by some authors is noted in the notice.

comments.author: Andrew Grey
comments.comment:
There are many concerns about the integrity of 172 publications by this research group, including this one. Some of the concerns are published
1. Anaesthesia 2020;75:1683–92, see Supplementary data. This paper is A149
2. Account Res 2020;28:149-61.
3. J Clin Epidemiol 2021;131:22-29.
Journals and publishers were notified of these concerns in July 2019. 18 publications have an expression of concern, and 6 have been retracted.
To our knowledge there has been no public response about any of the concerns. We think these publications are unreliable

comments.author: Hoya camphorifolia
comments.comment:
Retracted [19 November 2022](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s12011-022-03465-3). The Editors-in-Chief have retracted this article. After publication, several concerns have been raised about the integrity of this article. The article overlaps with another publication by the same author group [1] in terms of reported study timelines, location and sample size, but there is no cross-referencing. The following discrepancies were noted between the two studies: * This article does not mention any metformin treatment, whereas [1] reports that participants were taking 500 mg of metformin per day, increasing to 1500 mg/day over the first 3 weeks.
* This article does not mention stratification in the article, whereas [1] indicates that participants were matched for BMI, age, phenotypes A and D and then randomized.
* Smokers are only listed as an exclusion criterion in the current article. In addition, this article appears to contain some data errors.
* Under the “Study Design” section, it is stated that “Forty PCOS women were randomized (…)”, however, the article describes 60 participants elsewhere.
* In the first paragraph of the “Results” section, it is erroneously stated that 60 participants in each group completed the trial. Furthermore, the authors had previously published studies which reported that zinc and selenium supplementation improved clinical outcomes in women with polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) [2, 3]. As this clinical trial includes a placebo-controlled arm, concerns have been raised that potential beneficial treatments known to authors appear to have been withheld from this treatment group. An investigation into all the concerns was conducted by the National Committee for Ethics in Biomedical Research (NREC), Ministry of Health and Medical Education. The NREC concluded that there is insufficient evidence that the data was fabricated based on the summary statistics. In line with Iranian legal requirements, the results of their investigation were sent to the Kashan University of Medical Sciences (KAUMS) research ethics committee where Dr. Asemi is based. Of the specific concerns raised in relation to this article, the institution and authors confirmed that both this article and [1] were part of the same project, including inclusion and exclusion criteria, metformin treatment, and stratification. The authors stated that the two studies were differentiated by selecting different primary outcomes based on different biochemical variables. Further, the authors would like to correct the error within their article and confirm that the study included a total of 60 participants. The Editors have determined that the conclusions of this study are unreliable due to omissions in the description of the trial and the selective analysis of the same data set which was presented earlier in [1]. The authors Mehri Jamilian and Zatollah Asemi disagree with this retraction. The author Maryam Maktami has not responded to correspondence regarding this retraction. **References**
* [1] Jamilian M, Maktabi M, Asemi Z (2017) A trial on the effects of magnesium-zinc-calcium-vitamin D co-supplementation on glycemic control and markers of cardio-metabolic risk in women with polycystic ovary syndrome. Arch Iran Med 20(10):640–645
* [2] Jamilian M et al (2016) Effects of zinc supplementation on endocrine outcomes in women with polycystic ovary syndrome: a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial. Biol Trace Elem Res 170(2):271–278
* [3] Razavi M et al (2016) Selenium supplementation and the effects on reproductive outcomes, biomarkers of inflammation, and oxidative stress in women with polycystic ovary syndrome. Horm Metab Res 48(3):185–190

Commenters request confirmation of percentages and denominators used in reporting the number of affected reviews and retracted trials, as well as the count of citing publications and citations. The author responds by affirming corrections to a percentage calculation and explaining discrepancies arising from the timing of data acquisition. The exchange enhances clarity around the accuracy of reported figures and suggests an impending formal correction to the recent paper.

comments.author: Hedyotis minutopuberula
comments.comment: Previously, Avenell et al. (2019) concluded that the findings of 13/36 (36%) systematic reviews, clinical guidelines and other reviews would likely change if the retracted trials they cited were removed. Referring to: Avenell, A., Stewart, F., Grey, A., Gamble, G., & Bolland, M. (2019). An investigation into the impact and implications of published papers from retracted research: Systematic search of affected literature. BMJ Open, 9(10), e031909. However, in Table 2 of Avenell et al. (2019), it is indicated that the findings of 13/32 (or ~41%) of the findings of affected publications would likely change. Could the authors please check if it supposed to be 13/32 or 13/36, and thus, 36% or 41%.

comments.author: Hedyotis minutopuberula
comments.comment: PS 2022 paper: "Following suspicions aroused during the conduct of a Cochrane review (Avenell et al. 2009), 33 randomized trials by Yoshihiro Sato and Jun Iwamoto were investigated, and findings published (Bolland et al. 2016). Of these publications, twenty-eight were retracted between 2016–2019 in the field of osteoporosis" 2019 paper: "By May 2019, 27/33 of these affected trial reports had been retracted" Were 27 or 28 papers retracted?

comments.author: Hedyotis minutopuberula
comments.comment: PS 2 "By August 2021, 72 citing publications listed by WoS themselves had 10,493 citations, and 10 unlisted by WoS had 424 citations on Scopus. Of these 82 citing publications, 67 (82%) had at least one citation in 2021." Do the authors mean 72, or 82?

comments.author: Alison Avenell
comments.comment: Thank you for your questions and interest in our papers. Thank you for spotting my error in our 2022 paper. In our 2019 BMJ Open paper, in Table 2 13/32 (which is 41%) of affected papers had findings that would likely change. In our 2022 paper this is incorrectly stated as 13/36 (36%). I will ask Accountability in Research to correct our 2022 paper. The 2019 BMJ Open paper is correct – by April 2019, 27/33 of affected trial reports had been retracted. One further affected trial report was retracted later in 2019. Thus the 2022 paper is also correct, as the literature search took place later in 2019. In the 2022 paper, the number is 82: 72 publications were listed on Web of Science and an additional 10 publications were listed on Scopus but not listed on Web of Science, of which 67/82 (82%) had at least one citation in 2021. Alison Avenell

comments.author: Andrew Grey
comments.comment:
There are many concerns about the integrity of 172 publications by this research group, including this one. Some of the concerns are published
1. Anaesthesia 2020;75:1683–92, see Supplementary data. This paper is A34
2. Account Res 2020;28:149-61.
3. J Clin Epidemiol 2021;131:22-29.
Journals and publishers were notified of these concerns in July 2019. 23 publications have an expression of concern. To our knowledge there has been no public response about any of the concerns. We think these publications are unreliable

comments.author: Andrew Grey
comments.comment:
There are many concerns about the integrity of 172 publications by this research group, including this one. Some of the concerns are published
1. Anaesthesia 2020;75:1683–92, see Supplementary data. This paper is A164
2. Account Res 2020;28:149-61.
3. J Clin Epidemiol 2021;131:22-29.
Journals and publishers were notified of these concerns in July 2019. 18 publications have an expression of concern, and 6 have been retracted. To our knowledge there has been no public response about any of the concerns. We think these publications are unreliable

comments.author: Andrew Grey
comments.comment:
There are many concerns about the integrity of 172 publications by this research group, including this one. Some of the concerns are published
1. Anaesthesia 2020;75:1683–92, see Supplementary data. This paper is A103
2. Account Res 2020;28:149-61.
3. J Clin Epidemiol 2021;131:22-29.
Journals and publishers were notified of these concerns in July 2019. 23 publications have an expression of concern. To our knowledge there has been no public response about any of the concerns. We think these publications are unreliable

pubpeer_signal_analysis.detail: The discussion centers on concerns regarding the integrity and reliability of publications by the study's research group, referencing multiple sources and noting a lack of public response to raised issues. Additional comments focus on the identical standard error (SE) values reported for both control and treated groups in the study, questioning the statistical presentation and implications for interpreting within-group and between-group variability. Commenters recommend increased transparency and encourage the authors to share raw and group-specific data. No author responses or official publication status notices are present.

comments.author: Andrew Grey
comments.comment: There are many concerns about the integrity of 172 publications by this research group, including this one. Some of the concerns are published 1. Anaesthesia 2020;75:1683–92, see Supplementary data. This paper is A77 2. Account Res 2020;28:149-61. 3. J Clin Epidemiol 2021;131:22-29. Journals and publishers were notified of these concerns in July 2019. 23 publications have an expression of concern. To our knowledge there has been no public response about any of the concerns. We think these publications are unreliable

comments.author: Dysdera arabisenen
comments.comment:
[Image: Chart or data image from the publication]
The two groups have identical SE values across all parameters. I understand that the means reflect the difference between data taken before and after the intervention period.

comments.author: Dysdera arabisenen
comments.comment:
[Image: Chart or data image from the publication]
In all 3 studies, the SE values for “adjusted change” of FPG (mg/dL) are 1.7 for both control and treated groups. Similarly, the SE values for HDL adjusted change are 1.3 in all 6 groups (across 3 studies). In each of the 3 studies, control and treated groups have different means, but identical SE values across all measures. (expression of concern)

comments.author: Dysdera arabisenen
comments.comment: Update of #2: The reason the control and treated groups have identical SE values is that ANCOVA generates a single pooled error variance. While not statistically “wrong,” this mode of presentation can be misleading — it prevents readers from assessing the actual within-group and between-group variabilities in the dataset. The authors are encouraged to share raw data, and group-specific SE data.

pubpeer_signal_analysis.detail: The discussion centers on concerns regarding the integrity of 172 publications from the research group responsible for this study, including the publication at hand. Specific references are provided to published reports of these concerns, and it is noted that journals and publishers were notified in July 2019. Out of the flagged publications, 18 have an expression of concern, and 6 have been retracted. The commenter states that, to their knowledge, there has been no public response to these issues, and expresses the view that these publications are unreliable. No author responses or official publication status notices such as retraction or correction were present at the time of analysis.

comments.author: Andrew Grey
comments.comment:
There are many concerns about the integrity of 172 publications by this research group, including this one. Some of the concerns are published
1. Anaesthesia 2020;75:1683–92, see Supplementary data. This paper is A166
2. Account Res 2020;28:149-61.
3. J Clin Epidemiol 2021;131:22-29.
Journals and publishers were notified of these concerns in July 2019. 18 publications have an expression of concern, and 6 have been retracted. To our knowledge there has been no public response about any of the concerns. We think these publications are unreliable

comments.comment: This article has been retracted at the request of the journal editorial team. Significant concerns were raised by a third party about the integrity of the data and the reported findings in the article. When approached for an explanation, the authors have been cooperative in providing some responses and documents. To verify the reported findings, the article and the documents provided by the authors were further evaluated by the Ethics Editor and the journal editorial team. The journal editorial team and the Ethics Editor were unable to confirm the integrity of the data presented in tables and their main outcome was that the article's results and conclusions are unreliable. Therefore, as the editorial team no longer have confidence in the reported conclusions the decision has been made to retract the article. The authors listed in the publication have been informed. The authors do not agree with the retraction.

pubpeer_signal_analysis.detail: The discussion on this PubPeer page centers around concerns about data integrity and potential ethical issues in a series of publications by the same research group. The first commenter highlights widespread doubts about the reliability of 172 publications, citing expressions of concern and prior retractions. The second comment provides detailed information on the article’s retraction, outlining discrepancies in reporting study methodology and participant numbers, failure to mention key treatment and stratification information, and overlapping content with another publication without appropriate cross-referencing. The editors' investigation found insufficient evidence of data fabrication but concluded that the published results are unreliable. Two authors disputed the retraction while one did not respond. The overall academic discussion emphasizes questions around research transparency, accurate reporting, and data reliability.

comments.author: Andrew Grey
comments.comment:
There are many concerns about the integrity of 172 publications by this research group, including this one. Some of the concerns are published 1. Anaesthesia 2020;75:1683–92, see Supplementary data. This paper is A149
2. Account Res 2020;28:149-61.
3. J Clin Epidemiol 2021;131:22-29.
Journals and publishers were notified of these concerns in July 2019. 18 publications have an expression of concern, and 6 have been retracted. To our knowledge there has been no public response about any of the concerns. We think these publications are unreliable

comments.author: Hoya camphorifolia
comments.comment:
Retracted [19 November 2022](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s12011-022-03465-3). The Editors-in-Chief have retracted this article. After publication, several concerns have been raised about the integrity of this article. The article overlaps with another publication by the same author group [1] in terms of reported study timelines, location and sample size, but there is no cross-referencing. The following discrepancies were noted between the two studies:
* This article does not mention any metformin treatment, whereas [1] reports that participants were taking 500 mg of metformin per day, increasing to 1500 mg/day over the first 3 weeks.
* This article does not mention stratification in the article, whereas [1] indicates that participants were matched for BMI, age, phenotypes A and D and then randomized.
* Smokers are only listed as an exclusion criterion in the current article. In addition, this article appears to contain some data errors.
* Under the “Study Design” section, it is stated that “Forty PCOS women were randomized (…)”, however, the article describes 60 participants elsewhere.
* In the first paragraph of the “Results” section, it is erroneously stated that 60 participants in each group completed the trial. Furthermore, the authors had previously published studies which reported that zinc and selenium supplementation improved clinical outcomes in women with polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) [2, 3]. As this clinical trial includes a placebo-controlled arm, concerns have been raised that potential beneficial treatments known to authors appear to have been withheld from this treatment group. An investigation into all the concerns was conducted by the National Committee for Ethics in Biomedical Research (NREC), Ministry of Health and Medical Education. The NREC concluded that there is insufficient evidence that the data was fabricated based on the summary statistics. In line with Iranian legal requirements, the results of their investigation were sent to the Kashan University of Medical Sciences (KAUMS) research ethics committee where Dr. Asemi is based. Of the specific concerns raised in relation to this article, the institution and authors confirmed that both this article and [1] were part of the same project, including inclusion and exclusion criteria, metformin treatment, and stratification. The authors stated that the two studies were differentiated by selecting different primary outcomes based on different biochemical variables. Further, the authors would like to correct the error within their article and confirm that the study included a total of 60 participants. The Editors have determined that the conclusions of this study are unreliable due to omissions in the description of the trial and the selective analysis of the same data set which was presented earlier in [1]. The authors Mehri Jamilian and Zatollah Asemi disagree with this retraction. The author Maryam Maktami has not responded to correspondence regarding this retraction. **References**

comments.author: Andrew Grey
comments.comment:
There are many concerns about the integrity of 172 publications by this research group, including this one. Some of the concerns are published
1. Anaesthesia 2020;75:1683–92, see Supplementary data. This paper is A160
2. Account Res 2020;28:149-61.
3. J Clin Epidemiol 2021;131:22-29.
Journals and publishers were notified of these concerns in July 2019. 18 publications have an expression of concern, and 6 have been retracted. To our knowledge there has been no public response about any of the concerns. We think these publications are unreliable

comments.author: Andrew Grey
comments.comment:
There are many concerns about the integrity of 172 publications by this research group, including this one. Some of the concerns are published
1. Anaesthesia 2020;75:1683–92, see Supplementary data. This paper is A72
2. Account Res 2020;28:149-61.
3. J Clin Epidemiol 2021;131:22-29.
Journals and publishers were notified of these concerns in July 2019. 23 publications have an expression of concern.
To our knowledge there has been no public response about any of the concerns.
We think these publications are unreliable

pubpeer_signal_analysis.detail: The PubPeer discussion centers on concerns regarding the integrity of 172 publications from the research group responsible for the discussed article. The commenter references three published sources that detail these concerns and notes that journals and publishers were notified in July 2019. They report that 18 publications from the group have expressions of concern and 6 have been retracted, while no public response has addressed these issues. The reliability of the group's publications is questioned, especially in light of the expressed concerns.

comments.author: Andrew Grey
comments.comment:
There are many concerns about the integrity of 172 publications by this research group, including this one. Some of the concerns are published
1. Anaesthesia 2020;75:1683–92, see Supplementary data. This paper is A140
2. Account Res 2020;28:149-61.
3. J Clin Epidemiol 2021;131:22-29.
Journals and publishers were notified of these concerns in July 2019. 18 publications have an expression of concern, and 6 have been retracted. To our knowledge there has been no public response about any of the concerns. We think these publications are unreliable

The comment highlights the absence of any public response from the authors regarding these issues and concludes that these publications are considered unreliable. An official 'Expression of concern' status notice is present for this article.

comments.author: Andrew Grey
comments.comment:
There are many concerns about the integrity of 172 publications by this research group, including this one. Some of the concerns are published 1. Anaesthesia 2020;75:1683–92, see Supplementary data. This paper is A47
2. Account Res 2020;28:149-61.
3. J Clin Epidemiol 2021;131:22-29. Journals and publishers were notified of these concerns in July 2019. 23 publications have an expression of concern. To our knowledge there has been no public response about any of the concerns. We think these publications are unreliable

pubpeer_signal_analysis.detail: The primary academic discussion centers on concerns regarding the integrity of 172 publications from the research group associated with this article. The comment references three publications where related concerns are reported, highlights that journals and publishers were alerted in July 2019, and notes that 23 of the group's publications currently have an expression of concern. There is a consensus in the comment that, as of the date posted, there has been no public response addressing these concerns, and the reliability of the publications is questioned. Additionally, the page includes an official expression of concern status notice related to this publication.

comments.author: Andrew Grey
comments.comment:
There are many concerns about the integrity of 172 publications by this research group, including this one. Some of the concerns are published
1. Anaesthesia 2020;75:1683–92, see Supplementary data. This paper is A47
2. Account Res 2020;28:149-61.
3. J Clin Epidemiol 2021;131:22-29.
Journals and publishers were notified of these concerns in July 2019. 23 publications have an expression of concern. To our knowledge there has been no public response about any of the concerns. We think these publications are unreliable

comments.author: Andrew Grey
comments.comment:
There are many concerns about the integrity of 172 publications by this research group, including this one. Some of the concerns are published
1. Anaesthesia 2020;75:1683–92, see Supplementary data. This paper is A149
2. Account Res 2020;28:149-61.
3. J Clin Epidemiol 2021;131:22-29.
Journals and publishers were notified of these concerns in July 2019. 18 publications have an expression of concern, and 6 have been retracted. To our knowledge there has been no public response about any of the concerns. We think these publications are unreliable

comments.author: _Hoya camphorifolia_
comments.comment:
Retracted [19 November 2022](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s12011-022-03465-3). The Editors-in-Chief have retracted this article. After publication, several concerns have been raised about the integrity of this article. The article overlaps with another publication by the same author group [1] in terms of reported study timelines, location and sample size, but there is no cross-referencing. The following discrepancies were noted between the two studies: * This article does not mention any metformin treatment, whereas [1] reports that participants were taking 500 mg of metformin per day, increasing to 1500 mg/day over the first 3 weeks.
* This article does not mention stratification in the article, whereas [1] indicates that participants were matched for BMI, age, phenotypes A and D and then randomized.
* Smokers are only listed as an exclusion criterion in the current article. In addition, this article appears to contain some data errors. * Under the “Study Design” section, it is stated that “Forty PCOS women were randomized (…)”, however, the article describes 60 participants elsewhere.
* In the first paragraph of the “Results” section, it is erroneously stated that 60 participants in each group completed the trial. Furthermore, the authors had previously published studies which reported that zinc and selenium supplementation improved clinical outcomes in women with polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) [2, 3]. As this clinical trial includes a placebo-controlled arm, concerns have been raised that potential beneficial treatments known to authors appear to have been withheld from this treatment group. An investigation into all the concerns was conducted by the National Committee for Ethics in Biomedical Research (NREC), Ministry of Health and Medical Education. The NREC concluded that there is insufficient evidence that the data was fabricated based on the summary statistics. In line with Iranian legal requirements, the results of their investigation were sent to the Kashan University of Medical Sciences (KAUMS) research ethics committee where Dr. Asemi is based. Of the specific concerns raised in relation to this article, the institution and authors confirmed that both this article and [1] were part of the same project, including inclusion and exclusion criteria, metformin treatment, and stratification. The authors stated that the two studies were differentiated by selecting different primary outcomes based on different biochemical variables. Further, the authors would like to correct the error within their article and confirm that the study included a total of 60 participants. The Editors have determined that the conclusions of this study are unreliable due to omissions in the description of the trial and the selective analysis of the same data set which was presented earlier in [1]. The authors Mehri Jamilian and Zatollah Asemi disagree with this retraction. The author Maryam Maktami has not responded to correspondence regarding this retraction. **References**
* [1] Jamilian M, Maktabi M, Asemi Z (2017) A trial on the effects of magnesium-zinc-calcium-vitamin D co-supplementation on glycemic control and markers of cardio-metabolic risk in women with polycystic ovary syndrome. Arch Iran Med 20(10):640–645
* [2] Jamilian M et al (2016) Effects of zinc supplementation on endocrine outcomes in women with polycystic ovary syndrome: a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial. Biol Trace Elem Res 170(2):271–278
* [3] Razavi M et al (2016) Selenium supplementation and the effects on reproductive outcomes, biomarkers of inflammation, and oxidative stress in women with polycystic ovary syndrome. Horm Metab Res 48(3):185–190

comments.author: Andrew Grey
comments.comment:
There are many concerns about the integrity of 172 publications by this research group, including this one. Some of the concerns are published
1. Anaesthesia 2020;75:1683–92, see Supplementary data. This paper is A48
2. Account Res 2020;28:149-61.
3. J Clin Epidemiol 2021;131:22-29.
Journals and publishers were notified of these concerns in July 2019. 23 publications have an expression of concern. To our knowledge there has been no public response about any of the concerns. We think these publications are unreliable

comments.comment: Copy/pasted from: "Retraction Note: Vaginal progesterone for prevention of preterm labor in asymptomatic twin pregnancies with sonographic short cervix: a randomized clinical trial of efficacy and safety. Published: 27 July 2021. The Editor-in-Chief has retracted this article. Contrary to the statement in the article, the authors did not obtain approval from a research ethics committee before conducting this interventional randomized control trial and therefore this study is in breach of the Declaration of Helsinki [1] and the editorial policy of the Journal. Concerns about the data reported in the article are under investigation by the University of Mansoura. Waleed El-Refaie stated on behalf of all co-authors that they do not agree with this retraction. [1]. WMA Declaration of Helsinki—Ethical principles for medical research involving human subjects. "

comments.author: Andrew Grey
comments.comment:
There are many concerns about the integrity of 172 publications by this research group, including this one. Some of the concerns are published 1. Anaesthesia 2020;75:1683–92, see Supplementary data. This paper is A166
2. Account Res 2020;28:149-61.
3. J Clin Epidemiol 2021;131:22-29. Journals and publishers were notified of these concerns in July 2019. 18 publications have an expression of concern, and 6 have been retracted. To our knowledge there has been no public response about any of the concerns. We think these publications are unreliable

pubpeer_signal_analysis.detail: The discussion on this PubPeer page centers on concerns regarding the integrity and reliability of publications from the research group responsible for the retracted article on magnesium-zinc-calcium-vitamin D co-supplementation in women with polycystic ovary syndrome. The comments reference numerous prior concerns, including data integrity and lack of response from authors. A detailed comment cites the official retraction and outlines specific methodological inconsistencies, such as discrepancies in participant numbers, lack of mentioned metformin treatment or stratification, and differences between related publications. The retraction notice notes both institutional investigation outcomes and author disagreement with the retraction. The overall theme is a consensus on unreliability and documentation of official retraction.

comments.author: Andrew Grey
comments.comment:
There are many concerns about the integrity of 172 publications by this research group, including this one. Some of the concerns are published
1. Anaesthesia 2020;75:1683–92, see Supplementary data. This paper is A149
2. Account Res 2020;28:149-61.
3. J Clin Epidemiol 2021;131:22-29.
Journals and publishers were notified of these concerns in July 2019. 18 publications have an expression of concern, and 6 have been retracted. To our knowledge there has been no public response about any of the concerns. We think these publications are unreliable

comments.author: Hoya camphorifolia
comments.comment:
Retracted [19 November 2022](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s12011-022-03465-3). The Editors-in-Chief have retracted this article. After publication, several concerns have been raised about the integrity of this article. The article overlaps with another publication by the same author group [1] in terms of reported study timelines, location and sample size, but there is no cross-referencing. The following discrepancies were noted between the two studies: - This article does not mention any metformin treatment, whereas [1] reports that participants were taking 500 mg of metformin per day, increasing to 1500 mg/day over the first 3 weeks.
- This article does not mention stratification in the article, whereas [1] indicates that participants were matched for BMI, age, phenotypes A and D and then randomized.
- Smokers are only listed as an exclusion criterion in the current article. In addition, this article appears to contain some data errors.
- Under the “Study Design” section, it is stated that “Forty PCOS women were randomized (…)”, however, the article describes 60 participants elsewhere.
- In the first paragraph of the “Results” section, it is erroneously stated that 60 participants in each group completed the trial. Furthermore, the authors had previously published studies which reported that zinc and selenium supplementation improved clinical outcomes in women with polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) [2, 3]. As this clinical trial includes a placebo-controlled arm, concerns have been raised that potential beneficial treatments known to authors appear to have been withheld from this treatment group. An investigation into all the concerns was conducted by the National Committee for Ethics in Biomedical Research (NREC), Ministry of Health and Medical Education. The NREC concluded that there is insufficient evidence that the data was fabricated based on the summary statistics. In line with Iranian legal requirements, the results of their investigation were sent to the Kashan University of Medical Sciences (KAUMS) research ethics committee where Dr. Asemi is based. Of the specific concerns raised in relation to this article, the institution and authors confirmed that both this article and [1] were part of the same project, including inclusion and exclusion criteria, metformin treatment, and stratification. The authors stated that the two studies were differentiated by selecting different primary outcomes based on different biochemical variables. Further, the authors would like to correct the error within their article and confirm that the study included a total of 60 participants. The Editors have determined that the conclusions of this study are unreliable due to omissions in the description of the trial and the selective analysis of the same data set which was presented earlier in [1]. The authors Mehri Jamilian and Zatollah Asemi disagree with this retraction. The author Maryam Maktami has not responded to correspondence regarding this retraction. References
- [1] Jamilian M, Maktabi M, Asemi Z (2017) A trial on the effects of magnesium-zinc-calcium-vitamin D co-supplementation on glycemic control and markers of cardio-metabolic risk in women with polycystic ovary syndrome. Arch Iran Med 20(10):640–645
- [2] Jamilian M et al (2016) Effects of zinc supplementation on endocrine outcomes in women with polycystic ovary syndrome: a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial. Biol Trace Elem Res 170(2):271–278
- [3] Razavi M et al (2016) Selenium supplementation and the effects on reproductive outcomes, biomarkers of inflammation, and oxidative stress in women with polycystic ovary syndrome. Horm Metab Res 48(3):185–190

comments.author: Andrew Grey
comments.comment:
There are many concerns about the integrity of 172 publications by this research group, including this one. Some of the concerns are published 1. Anaesthesia 2020;75:1683–92, see Supplementary data. This paper is A72
2. Account Res 2020;28:149-61.
3. J Clin Epidemiol 2021;131:22-29. Journals and publishers were notified of these concerns in July 2019. 23 publications have an expression of concern. To our knowledge there has been no public response about any of the concerns. We think these publications are unreliable

comments.author: Andrew Grey
comments.comment:
There are many concerns about the integrity of 172 publications by this research group, including this one. Some of the concerns are published
1. Anaesthesia 2020;75:1683–92, see Supplementary data. This paper is A161
2. Account Res 2020;28:149-61.
3. J Clin Epidemiol 2021;131:22-29.
Journals and publishers were notified of these concerns in July 2019. 18 publications have an expression of concern, and 6 have been retracted. To our knowledge there has been no public response about any of the concerns. We think these publications are unreliable

comments.author: Andrew Grey
comments.comment:
There are many concerns about the integrity of 172 publications by this research group, including this one. Some of the concerns are published
1. Anaesthesia 2020;75:1683–92, see Supplementary data. This paper is A166
2. Account Res 2020;28:149-61.
3. J Clin Epidemiol 2021;131:22-29.
Journals and publishers were notified of these concerns in July 2019. 18 publications have an expression of concern, and 6 have been retracted. To our knowledge there has been no public response about any of the concerns. We think these publications are unreliable

pubpeer_signal_analysis.detail: The single comment on this PubPeer page highlights serious concerns regarding the integrity of a large number of publications (172) by the same research group as the publication under discussion. The commenter, Andrew Grey, cites several published articles where concerns are documented and notes that journals and publishers were notified in July 2019. content.author: Ben Goldacre
content.content:
This trial has the wrong trial registry ID associated with it on PubMed: both in the XML on PubMed, and in the body of the text of the article. The ID given is NCT0151529. We believe the correct ID, which we have found by hand searching, is NCT01515293.

This comment is being posted as part of the OpenTrials.net project[1], an open database threading together all publicly accessible documents and data on each trial, globally. In the course of creating the database, and matching documents and data sources about trials from different locations, we have identified various anomalies in datasets such as PubMed, and in published papers. Alongside documenting the prevalence of problems, we are also attempting to correct these errors and anomalies wherever possible, by feeding back to the originators. We have corrected this data in the OpenTrials.net database; we hope that this trial’s text and metadata can also be corrected at source, in PubMed and in the accompanying paper.

Many thanks,

Jessica Fleminger, Ben Goldacre*

[1] Goldacre, B., Gray, J., 2016. OpenTrials: towards a collaborative open database of all available information on all clinical trials. Trials 17. doi:10.1186/s13063-016-1290-8

data.label: Does the study have an associated retraction?
data.comment: No retraction on journal website, agree with INSPECT-AI suggestion.

data.label: Does the study have an associated expression of concern or other relevant post publication notice?
data.comment:
Checked journal website and there is an expression of concern: https://doi.org/10.1159/000529289
Concerns raised regarding discrepancies in trial registration, undeclared conflict of interests and data presented. An investigation is currently ongoing. INSPECT-AI also identified a comment on PubPeer regarding concerns with this research group.

data.label: Is there evidence of concerning patterns in the publication history of authors?
data.comment: INSPECT-AI has identified that both authors have multiple articles retracted or with expressions of concerns on retraction watch. There are concerns with this research term.

data.label: Are there concerns relating to the timing or absence of study registration?
data.comment:
In WHO database, the data of first enrollment is 2015-02-02, which isn't picked up by INSPECT-AI. The data of registration is 2015-02-09 which is a week later than first enrollment. The entry also states 'No' for prospective registration. This alone may not cause concern as it's only a week out, and the dates given in paper do align with the details on the registration entry.
Hence, I agree with the INSPECT-AI suggestion. (Do note that it's unlikely that this study would progress to this check as it would have been excluded at the first stage due to serious concerns, relating to the expression of concern and multiple retractions of papers by the same research team).
Article has an expression of concern due to the integrity of the data. Both authors have multiple articles retracted or with expressions of concerns on retraction watch.

Specifically, every 101 records, in almost every case the following variables are identical: WBC, Hb, Plt, BUN, Cr, Na, BS, TOTALCHO, LDL, HDL, TG, PT, INR, PTT These identical 14 values occur consistently for groups of four (or occasionally three, since the sample size is a little less than 404), patients. This does not seem very likely to have happened by chance. This can be seen by creating a variable that is the "obs_id" (patient ID number) modulo 101, and sorting on it, as in this extract: [Image: screenshot of spreadsheet with repeating numerical patterns] 2. Brown", "date": "November 2025", "links": [], "is_reply": false, "reply_to": null, "is_author_response": false }, { "id": 48, "comment": "As per #45, there is an EOC: "The BMJ was alerted to post-publication discussion raising concerns about a variety of issues; some issues were apparent from the data that support the paper, and are linked to from the article. Examples of the issues identified include irregularities in the data, concern about the inclusion of participants who did not meet the age criteria specified in the study, and concerns about undeclared conflicts of interest and authorship. Reason for expressing concern The editors judge that the trial may have breached accepted practices and that the results may not be reliable. Further actions The BMJ’s content integrity team will take up the concerns with the authors, and investigate fully—involving institutions and regulatory authorities as necessary. The authors have informed the journal that an auditable replacement dataset has been prepared and will be made available to The BMJ. The BMJ will update this notice and make a decision about what post-publication change to the content is needed." This response seems to encapsulate much of what is wrong with the system for dealing with publication integrity concerns. It is abundantly clear from the above thread that the data for the participant characteristics are unreliable. The paper should be retracted now because it is clear the results cannot be relied upon. There is sufficient evidence to permit this action. Separately, an investigation can be undertaken as to why this problem happened, but retraction should not be dependent upon that outcome nor wait for it to be completed.", "author": "Mark J Bolland", "date": "November 2025", "links": [], "is_reply": false, "reply_to": null, "is_author_response": false } // NOTE: Dozens more comments follow this detailed structure but are omitted here for brevity. ], "summary": "The discussion thread on this PubPeer entry includes extensive and detailed post-publication scrutiny of a phase 3 clinical trial (PREVENT-TAHA8) published in BMJ. Early comments focus on inconsistencies between the registered trial protocol and the published dataset, especially regarding age eligibility, sample size, and outcome reporting. Multiple commenters identify highly regular and repetitive patterns in baseline and laboratory data, including variables such as WBC, Hb, Plt, and anthropometric measures, which do not appear plausible biologically and statistically.

Author responses acknowledge recognition of inconsistencies and promise an internal audit and later clarification. However, further analysis by independent commentators, including methodologists and clinicians, documents additional irregularities in the data (such as repeated values, unlikely distributions, variables possibly mislabeled, and outcome variables inconsistent with reported timelines). Additional comments highlight undeclared conflicts of interest and significant authorship and peer-review process anomalies, including the addition of international authors with operational roles not evidently feasible due to geographic constraints, and evidence that peer review may have bypassed the most critical reviewers at revision.

A notice of Expression of Concern has been issued by the journal but, as discussed by several commenters, the underlying data's unreliability has led to calls for retraction according to COPE guidelines, rather than correction with a new dataset. Commentary also explores broader editorial and publication ethics issues, and the case is used as an example to question the effectiveness of data sharing and journal quality control. Almost all analysis is accompanied by technical breakdowns, code links, or image documentation. No retraction or correction notice aside from the Expression of Concern had been posted at the time of this extraction. No parsing errors were encountered."
}

comments.author: Andrew Grey
comments.comment:
There are many concerns about the integrity of 172 publications by this research group, including this one. Some of the concerns are published
1. Anaesthesia 2020;75:1683–92, see Supplementary data. This paper is A132
2. Account Res 2020;28:149-61.
3. J Clin Epidemiol 2021;131:22-29. Journals and publishers were notified of these concerns in July 2019. 18 publications have an expression of concern, and 6 have been retracted. To our knowledge there has been no public response about any of the concerns. We think these publications are unreliable

comments.author: Elisabeth M Bik
comments.comment: Expression of Concern, found here: "This Expression of Concern is for the above article, published online on 27 June 2018 in Wiley Online Library (wileyonlinelibrary.com), and has been published by agreement between the journal Editor-in-Chief, Rainer Spanagel, Society for the Study of Addiction, and John Wiley & Sons Ltd. The Expression of Concern has been agreed due to concerns raised regarding the integrity of the research and discrepancies in reporting. An investigation has been conducted by the National Committee for Ethics in Biomedical Research Iran, in coordination with Kashan University of Medical Sciences (KAUMS). However, without the verification of clinical records there remain sufficient doubts about the feasibility and integrity of the research undertaken. As a result, the journal has decided to issue an Expression of Concern to alert readers."

There are many concerns about the integrity of 172 publications by this research group, including this one. Some of the concerns are published

data.label: Are there concerns relating to the timing or absence of study registration?
data.comment: On trial registry, date of registration is 22/6/2015 and date of first enrollment is 02/06/2015. It also states 'No' to 'Prospective registration'. In the publication it states the study was carried out between June and September 2015 (not that recruitment occured until September 2015). The study was only 12 weeks long, so it is likely most (if not all) participants were recruited in June and this could of occurred before the trial was registered on 22nd June. Therefore, there are concerns about timing of registration.

Study has an expression of concern on the journal website about research integrity. Also a comment posted on PubPeer about this research team and also nearly all authors are mentioned on Retraction Watch. Concerns about timing of registration and recruitment of participants.

The commenter enumerates references to published concerns and expresses doubt about the reliability of the group's publications, noting that journals and publishers have been notified and that some have issued expressions of concern. No author response or public clarification appears to have been provided, and there are no official publication status notices present on the page.

comments.author: Andrew Grey
comments.comment:
There are many concerns about the integrity of 172 publications by this research group, including this one. Some of the concerns are published
1. Anaesthesia 2020;75:1683–92, see Supplementary data. This paper is A72
2. Account Res 2020;28:149-61.
3. J Clin Epidemiol 2021;131:22-29.
Journals and publishers were notified of these concerns in July 2019. 23 publications have an expression of concern. To our knowledge there has been no public response about any of the concerns. We think these publications are unreliable

comments.author: Andrew Grey
comments.comment:
There are many concerns about the integrity of 172 publications by this research group, including this one. Some of the concerns are published
1. Anaesthesia 2020;75:1683–92, see Supplementary data. This paper is A132
2. Account Res 2020;28:149-61.
3. J Clin Epidemiol 2021;131:22-29.
Journals and publishers were notified of these concerns in July 2019. 18 publications have an expression of concern, and 6 have been retracted. To our knowledge there has been no public response about any of the concerns. We think these publications are unreliable

comments.author: Elisabeth M Bik
comments.comment: Expression of Concern, found here: "This Expression of Concern is for the above article, published online on 27 June 2018 in Wiley Online Library (wileyonlinelibrary.com), and has been published by agreement between the journal Editor-in-Chief, Rainer Spanagel, Society for the Study of Addiction, and John Wiley & Sons Ltd. The Expression of Concern has been agreed due to concerns raised regarding the integrity of the research and discrepancies in reporting. An investigation has been conducted by the National Committee for Ethics in Biomedical Research Iran, in coordination with Kashan University of Medical Sciences (KAUMS). However, without the verification of clinical records there remain sufficient doubts about the feasibility and integrity of the research undertaken. As a result, the journal has decided to issue an Expression of Concern to alert readers."

pubpeer_signal_analysis.detail: The PubPeer page for this publication contains one comment by Andrew Grey, raising serious concerns about the integrity of 172 publications from the research group responsible for this study, including the present article. The commenter cites references to other publications and supplementary data where such concerns have been documented. It is noted that journals and publishers were notified in July 2019; several publications have received expressions of concern or have been retracted, yet no public response from the authors has been identified. As of the comment's date, the reliability of the involved publications is called into question. There are no replies, no author responses, and no official publication status notices such as retractions or corrections for this article.

comments.author: Andrew Grey
comments.comment:
There are many concerns about the integrity of 172 publications by this research group, including this one. Some of the concerns are published 1. Anaesthesia 2020;75:1683–92, see Supplementary data. This paper is A164
2. Account Res 2020;28:149-61.
3. J Clin Epidemiol 2021;131:22-29. Journals and publishers were notified of these concerns in July 2019. 18 publications have an expression of concern, and 6 have been retracted. To our knowledge there has been no public response about any of the concerns. We think these publications are unreliable

comments.author: Andrew Grey
comments.comment:
There are many concerns about the integrity of 172 publications by this research group, including this one. Some of the concerns are published
1. Anaesthesia 2020;75:1683–92, see Supplementary data. This paper is A28
2. Account Res 2020;28:149-61.
3. J Clin Epidemiol 2021;131:22-29.
Journals and publishers were notified of these concerns in July 2019. 23 publications have an expression of concern.
To our knowledge there has been no public response about any of the concerns. We think these publications are unreliable

comments.author: Psilocladia obliquata
comments.comment:
A quick view shows inconsistencies as you can't loose probands to follow-up and report a change from baseline. [Image: file illustrating possible data inconsistencies]

comments.author: Andrew Grey
comments.comment:
There are many concerns about the integrity of 172 publications by this research group, including this one. Some of the concerns are published
1. Anaesthesia 2020;75:1683–92, see Supplementary data. This paper is A140
2. Account Res 2020;28:149-61.
3. J Clin Epidemiol 2021;131:22-29.
Journals and publishers were notified of these concerns in July 2019. 18 publications have an expression of concern, and 6 have been retracted. To our knowledge there has been no public response about any of the concerns. We think these publications are unreliable

pubpeer_signal_analysis.detail: The discussion centers on concerns regarding the integrity of 172 publications authored by the research group, including the indexed clinical trial. The main comment highlights that various journals and publishers were alerted to these concerns, leading to expressions of concern on 18 publications and six retractions. There is no evidence of an author response or official publication status notices in the form of retraction or correction statements.

comments.author: Andrew Grey
comments.comment:
There are many concerns about the integrity of 172 publications by this research group, including this one. Some of the concerns are published
1. Anaesthesia 2020;75:1683–92, see Supplementary data. This paper is A166
2. Account Res 2020;28:149-61.
3. J Clin Epidemiol 2021;131:22-29.
Journals and publishers were notified of these concerns in July 2019. 18 publications have an expression of concern, and 6 have been retracted. To our knowledge there has been no public response about any of the concerns. We think these publications are unreliable

pubpeer_signal_analysis.detail: The PubPeer discussion centers on the retraction of a clinical trial investigating the effects of ivermectin on SARS-CoV-2 positive subjects. The retraction notice cites an error in the files used for statistical analysis, with all parties, including the authors, the institution, and the journal, agreeing there was no ethical breach. Elisabeth M Bik summarizes the retraction and references external media highlighting data duplication concerns. Author Ali A. Samaha affirms the absence of ethical violations, framing the error as unintentional and expressing concern about the reputational impact of ongoing PubPeer comments. Another user, Hoya camphorifolia, questions the journal’s basis for asserting the error was accidental and clarifies that PubPeer often hosts discussions about various issues beyond deliberate misconduct. The main discussion themes include the distinction between honest errors and unethical behavior, journal transparency in communicating retraction reasons, and the broader role of PubPeer in scientific discourse.

comments.author: Elisabeth M Bik
comments.comment: October 2021 retraction: "The journal retracts the article, Effects of a Single Dose of Ivermectin on Viral and Clinical Outcomes in Asymptomatic SARS-CoV-2 Infected Subjects: A Pilot Clinical Trial in Lebanon [1], cited above. Following publication, the authors contacted the editorial office regarding an error between files used for the statistical analysis. Adhering to our complaints procedure, an investigation was conducted that confirmed the error reported by the authors. This retraction was approved by the Editor in Chief of the journal. The authors agreed to this retraction." Retraction Watch coverage: Also see this BBC article from October 2021: From that article: "A recent study in Lebanon was found to have blocks of details of 11 patients that had been copied and pasted repeatedly - suggesting many of the trial's apparent patients didn't really exist."

comments.author: Ali A. Samaha
comments.comment: Independent investigations by the team, institutional and the journal review ALL confirmed that there was no ethical violation. It was a simple error in the files used for the analysis. The authors had the moral and professional courage to retract the paper. Adding comments on pubpeer will be construed as though there were ethical violations. This site is intended to uncover or question data that may appear to have been falsified, fabricated or obtained via unethical routes. None of these are in this paper. So, keeping this comment will tarnish the reputation of the authors for no valid reason. Thank you.

comments.author: Hoya camphorifolia
comments.comment: #2 How could the journal confirm that errors in the data were accidental? Have the editors announced this finding? It is not in the Retraction Note. _"This site is intended to uncover or question data that may appear to have been falsified, fabricated or obtained via unethical routes"_ I cannot speak for the intentions of PubPeer's architects, but I don't believe this is true. People often leave comments about innocent errors in figure assembly, or even to comment positively on papers that deserve wider attention or have corollaries that deserve further exploration.

comments.author: Andrew Grey
comments.comment:
There are many concerns about the integrity of 172 publications by this research group, including this one. Some of the concerns are published
1. Anaesthesia 2020;75:1683–92, see Supplementary data. This paper is A161
2. Account Res 2020;28:149-61.
3. J Clin Epidemiol 2021;131:22-29.
Journals and publishers were notified of these concerns in July 2019. 18 publications have an expression of concern, and 6 have been retracted. To our knowledge there has been no public response about any of the concerns. We think these publications are unreliable
